title: eval-harness: CI hooks and metric integrations for per-prompt regression gating
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: We need stronger per-prompt regression detection in CI to prevent subtle quality regressions from rolling out. This PR adds per-prompt CI hooks, integrates eval-harness metrics into our CI pipeline, and exposes a lightweight exporter for threshold-based gating. Motivation: ENG-2134 requires prompt-level visibility and automatic gating for high-risk prompt-sets. Changes: - New per-prompt runner that executes a curated prompt set subset in CI and emits metrics (latency, pass-rate, top-k accuracy) - Metric exporter that uploads results to the eval-metrics service and writes a local artifact for CI gating - CircleCI job updates and helper scripts to run the per-prompt checks in parallel shards - Documentation for authors and owners on adding prompt-sets and configuring thresholds - Tests and flake fixes for existing eval harness tests Checklist: - [x] Implement per-prompt runner and metric exporter - [x] Add CircleCI job and scripts - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Add docs and runbook - [x] Validation against a small sample of prompt-sets on staging - [x] Add Linear links to PR (ENG-2134, ENG-2190) Testing notes: Ran the full eval-harness suite on a dedicated runner; per-prompt checks ran in 3 parallel shards and completed in ~12 minutes. Exporter validated against a test endpoint. Rollout: Feature is backward compatible; gates are opt-in via repo-level config. If thresholds fail, the job fails the build and uploads the artifact for triage. Related: previous work on per-prompt metrics in ENG-2041 and the eval-harness refactor (ENG-1987).
